get_file_rows.description: Read the data inside one of the portal's files, such as a CSV, without downloading it: search its rows for words, keep only the rows whose columns hold given values, choose the columns, order and page through them. Works on any file whose is_queryable is true, which 'Get a dataset' and 'Get a file' report and which most of Madrid's CSV files are. Every answer also lists the file's columns and how many rows matched.
get_file_rows.display_str_template: Get the rows of Open Data Madrid file {0}.
get_file_rows.name: get_file_rows

parameters.description: The file's id, or a link to it. 'Get a dataset' and 'Search files' return the id of every file, such as 212411-0-madrid-avisa-csv; a file's title will not do.
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: Only rows containing these words in any column, in the file's own order unless 'Order by column' is set. Leave blank to read every row.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only rows whose columns hold exactly these values: a column's name, and the value it must hold. Matching is exact, capitals and accents included, so copy a value from a row rather than retyping it. A list of values keeps rows holding any of them.
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Only these columns, in this order. Leave blank for all of them. Names must match the file's own, which every answer lists under columns.
parameters.name: columns

parameters.description: Return each different row once. With 'Columns' set to DISTRITO, this lists the districts that appear in the file. Off by default.
parameters.name: distinct

parameters.description: The column to order the rows by. Leave blank to keep the file's own order. A column stored as text orders as text does, so 10 comes before 9. Rows that tie keep the file's own order, so reading on with 'Skip' never repeats or misses one.
parameters.name: order_by

parameters.description: Which way to order by that column. Defaults to ascending.
parameters.name: direction

parameters.description: How many rows to return (1 to 1000). Defaults to 100. Use 'Skip' alongside it to read further into the file.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: How many matching rows to skip before returning any. Defaults to 0. Set it to the number already read to fetch the next page.
parameters.name: offset

get_file_rows.result_str_template: Open Data Madrid file rows retrieved.

columns.description: Every column of the file, or the chosen ones, in order. _id is each row's position in the file, and rank how well it matched when searching for words.

name.description: The column's name, exactly as filters and ordering want it.

type.description: How the portal stores the column: text, int, numeric or timestamp. Most of Madrid's files store every column as text.

file.description: The id of the file the rows were read from.

offset.description: How many matching rows were skipped.

result_count.description: How many rows came back in this answer.

rows.description: The rows, each a record keyed by column name.

total_count.description: How many rows match in the whole file, which says whether there is another page to read.

total_is_estimate.description: Whether the portal estimated total_count rather than counting, which it may do for a very large file.

search_datasets.description: Search the whole Madrid catalogue by words in a dataset's title, description or tags, and narrow it by category, tag, file format or publishing body. Picking several values for one filter widens the result (any of them matches); filling in different filters narrows it (all of them must match). Leave the words blank to browse a filter on its own: every dataset tagged 'movilidad', say, or every dataset updated since a given day. Each result comes back with its files, formats, licence and when it was last updated.
